summary: Melange is a ZX Spectrum invitation production by Light Future and 4th Dimension, first in the Invitation compo at Chaos Constructions 2000. CyberJack did the code, Diver the graphics and MmcM the music.
why: An invitation that won its compo. Key-Jee is credited with fixing some of the music patterns.

summary: A Commodore PET demo by Shiru, first in the LowEnd Demo (Combined) compo at CAFe 2022.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2023.

summary: Noice's Atari VCS (2600) demo, first in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. Shadow did the code and Ilmarque the music.
why: A compo winner with a two-person credit list.

summary: Onslaught's C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Flashback 2014. Algorithm and Conjuror did the code, SoNiC and Algorithm the music, and the credits list five graphics artists.
why: Sceners single out the line shadow circle, the tile twister and the streamed music at the end. Full credits and a description of each part are in the note program on side 1.

quote.text: Enjoyed the show, particularly the shadow circle and end part.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2017. Gasman is credited with code, music, graphics and text. It uses the ZX multicolour mode and has a Berlin tag.
why: A compo winner made by one person. The multicolour mode is the thing to watch for.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's VIC-20 demo, first in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2003. Viznut did the code, graphics and music. It's tagged for speech synthesis.
why: Nominated for Best 4k Intro at the 2003 Scene.org Awards. Listen for the speech synthesis.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's C64 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2012. Viznut did the code, text and graphics, with more graphics by ccr and Parkitus and music by Ilmarque. It's tagged politics and anticapitalism.
why: Commenters call it unstable, violent and glitchy, and mean it as praise. Some enjoy the intentionally broken parts and the interference part, and one calls it an interesting concept.

quote.text: Unstable, violent & glitchy. A successful experiment!!

summary: Kiss Kill is a ZX Spectrum demo by Candy Says and Gasman that won the Wild compo at DiHalt 2013.
why: A wild compo winner. There are no credits or comments on the sheet, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Genesis Project's demo for the Enterprise 128, first in the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2016. Shadow did the code, Illmidus the graphics and Jason C. Brooke the music.
why: A compo winner for the Enterprise 128.

summary: A NES/Famicom 64K intro by Excess Team, deMarche and Mega Cat, made as an invitation to CAFe 2019. Third in Wild at TokyoDemoFest 2018 and second in the CAFePARTY 2019 Invitations at CAFe 2019.
why: It placed in two compos. Adam Bazaroff did the graphics, Nik-O the music, and mr287cc and TmK the code. The source is available.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. It's tagged 256k. Ajcek and Szeryf did the code, At0m, Gepard and Odyn1ec the graphics and Wieczor the music.
why: A compo winner and the group's second Silly Venture win in a row after Boogie Nights in 2012.

summary: Bitshifters' demo for the BBC Micro, tagged for the BBC Master, that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2018. KieranHJ did the code and effects, Henley the music code and Atari ST YM port, and Mad Max the music. The source is available.
why: A compo winner, with the music coming over from the Atari ST's YM sound chip.

summary: ISO is an Atari VCS (2600) demo by JAC, first in the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11. JAC did the code and graphics and Jakub Husak the music. The source is available.
why: A compo winner. JAC also won the Atari 8-bit compo at Silly Venture 2k10 with Silly Things.

summary: Origo Dreamline's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at the Light and Phenomena Easter Party 1992. Mixer and CLF did the code, with music by Zardax and Mixer and graphics from BX, Fox, Gordon and Crony.
why: Commenters call it the first real trackmo on the C64 and say it was far ahead of its time in 1992. They single out the filled vectors, the real-time Mandelbrot fractals and Zardax's tunes.

quote.text: It was a real jaw dropper when it was released.

summary: Machined is a ZX Spectrum 128 demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, third in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. The video is the final version.
why: A podium finish at Sundown. The fact sheet has no credits, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Xenon's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at X 2008. WVL and Megabrain did the code, A-Man and Arne the music, and Electric, Oxbow, Sander and Valsary the graphics.
why: Sceners single out the animated pig part, the 3D scroller and how closely the effects follow the music. One says it has the best soundtrack of the X 2008 demo entries.

quote.text: great partydemo! i especially dig the (outstanding) music sync with the visual effects, which can be found everywhere throughout the demo.

summary: Triple Threat is an Atari 8-bit demo by Mystic Bytes, Noice and Agenda, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. Shadow did the code, Ripek the graphics and BeWu the music.
why: A three-group collaboration that finished one place behind Lamers' Gene.

summary: Resource's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at X 2001. Oswald did the code, with graphics by AmN and Sander and music by Dane, GRG and Mitch. It uses the Krill loader.
why: Resource's own notes say the house came down at X 2001. Commenters call it a milestone, with an epic soundtrack, Amiga-style effects, and bump mapping and a light mask that stand out.

quote.text: This really is one of the highlights of c64 demos ever. It has power, it has show, it has everything.

summary: SHAPE's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2014. GRG did code and music, Knut code, Archmage the graphics and Kristian music. Tagged for plasma, a tunnel, sine dots and bobs.
why: Sceners praise it as a demo with a message, with Archmage's disturbing artwork and a haunting soundtrack. It manages all this on a single disk side.

quote.text: The effects and soundtrack go hand in hand with the awesome graphics.

summary: The final 100% version of Booze Design's Royal Arte for the C64. HCL did the code and graphics, with more graphics by DeeKay, Forbidden Cult and Valsary and music from six musicians.
why: Commenters single out the sprite FPP effect, the smooth DYPP screen, and the border scrollers. It's a demo people say they keep going back to.

quote.text: this is such a great demo! i keep on watching it, equally amazed every time.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at The Party 1995. It is a single file of about 35 KB containing three hidden parts. Graham did the code, Biz Kid and Sire the graphics and Jeff the music.
why: Ranked 15th best demo in Design #1 in 1997. Commenters praise the music, the bitmapped vector rotator and the fast horizontal scaling, and one remembers seeing it live as a turning point.

quote.text: This demo made a huge impression on me. Still looks and sounds amazing

summary: Arise and Joker's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at the speccy.pl party 2023.1. Wacek and Luke did the code, Bimber and Wacek the graphics, and Pator and MCH the music.
why: Nominated for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023 and tagged for the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy invitation to Alternative Party 2009, which won the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2009. Äkknäkk did the graphics and Maitotuote the code. The video is live footage from the compo.
why: A compo winner on the Game Boy, tagged as using the Carillon player.

summary: A multi-group Amstrad CPC megademo by Futurs', GPA, Pulpo Corrosivo, Vanity, Benediction, Dirty Minds and Shinra, titled for 30 years of the Amstrad. It's tagged as a sprites record.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at the Meteoriks 2017. The credits list eight coders, plus a large team of artists and musicians.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2013. drwho and Lovebeam did the code, and Sweetbutt the graphics and music.
why: A compo winner made by a team of three.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo, second in the Demo compo at X 2004. Clarence did the code, Leon the graphics and DRAX and Fanta the music. This is a hardware capture.
why: Commenters like the old-school code, the rasterbars and the elephant picture, though some feel parts run long.

quote.text: Excellent demo. Nice music, graphics and code. And the elephant picture is sublime.

summary: Crescent's 256-byte intro for the C64: an interactive raycaster, written by Wisdom. The source is available.
why: It made the Slashdot front page in 2013, and commenters were amazed to see a raycaster fit in so little.

quote.text: I've been impressed by some 1k js effects recently and was thinking, no way could the c64 do the same, but here I am proven wrong

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, sixth in the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2011 and nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. Pantaloon, Hollowman, Abaddon and Alfatech did the code and Louie the graphics.
why: Sceners enjoy its humour, especially the extra-large Mario part and the graffiti train. One was surprised it placed so low.

quote.text: Hilarious extra-large Mario part and nice idea about the street art going on the trains.

summary: Bandwagon's MSX demo that won the Demo compo at Plutonium 2000. nf did the code, Mermaid and Scythe the graphics and Gspot the music.
why: A compo winner on the MSX. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Bonzai's three-disk-side C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at X 2018 and nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2019. It has a hidden part and a humorous streak.
why: One scener's favourite of the whole compo; others praise its design, transitions and soundtrack. Burglar picks out the shade scroller, the diagonal charset scroller and the huge parallax logo.

quote.text: Design, transitions, editing and soundtrack just ooze of impossible awesomeness!

summary: Camelot's Tower Power for the C64, here in its 100% version. Slammer did the code, Jeff the music and music player, and four artists did the graphics. A note is on disk 1.
why: Commenters call it the trackmo of its era and praise the vectors, the vector fly-ins and the colour snakes in the round vector part. It placed joint sixth in a 1997 Design ranking of best demos.
highlights: colour snakes in round vector part

quote.text: This was THE Trackmo for a long time. In line with demos from Black Mail, Brutal, Crest and other groups, this was probably the demo that helped shape the 1990s.

summary: Large Unified Theory is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, first in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2010. Viznut is credited with the code.
why: A compo winner on the VIC-20 with a single credit, for Viznut's code.

summary: A three-disk-side C64 demo by Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, third in the Demo compo at X 2014. Pantaloon, Perplex, Puterman, Stein, Bjørn, Che and Zaphod share the code, with graphics by Pal and music by OMP.
why: Sceners praise the consistent theme, the transitions and the zoom boxes between parts, and Prosonix's big soundtrack. One felt the music and visuals didn't sync up.

quote.text: The consistent theme and nice transitions ties the effects together beautifully.

summary: Taboo's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Visual Party 4.0 in 1994. This is the 50% version.
why: Ranked 11th best demo in Design #1 in February 1997.

summary: Singular Crew's C64 demo that won the Wild Demo / Animation compo at Function 2017. It needs four C64s running in sync. Scorpy and Soci did the code, Poison and Leon the graphics and Vincenzo the music.
why: Sceners like the idea and how well it is executed, and are impressed that four machines stay in sync.

quote.text: Splendid idea, well executed.

summary: Life On Mars's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2014. introspec did the design and code, Diver the graphics and Fatal Snipe the music. This is the party version.
why: A compo winner that was designed and coded by one person.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Vanity, first in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2020. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Tom&Jerry the music.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2021: a full intro with music in 4096 bytes.

summary: Dirty Minds' Amstrad CPC demo that won the Wild Demo compo at Forever 2012. Optimus did the code, Voxfreax the graphics and Sice the music.
why: A wild compo winner on the CPC. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Genesis Project's Sega Master System demo, seventh in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Shadow did the code, Illmidus the graphics and NightBeat the music.
why: Little else is on record. The same group also made the Enterprise demo First Contact.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s demo for the C64 DTV, which won the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Streetuff did code, graphics and text, with more code from Benson and Peiselulli, graphics by Spotter and music by Linus.
why: Commenters note TRSI keeping the DTV moving with a major demo, and single out the hires graphics, the vectors, the tunnel and the MOD player. One would have liked more dynamic part linking.

quote.text: MOD-player was cool, aswell as the highres vectors and tunnel and etc. etc :)

summary: Ate Bit's invitation to Sundown 2006 for the ZX Spectrum. evilpaul did the code and graphics, with music by Matt Furniss.
why: It won Most Original Concept at the 2006 Scene.org Awards and was also nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

summary: Overlanders' Amstrad CPC demo, whose video title mentions 50Hz and 4k. Madram did the code, Beb the graphics and Shap the music.
why: The music credits also list Ben Daglish, Rob Hubbard, David Whittaker, Geoff Follin, Tim Follin and Wally Beben, a long list of composers for a single CPC demo.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at X 1995. Quiss did the code and PVCF the music.
why: Ranked first best demo in Design #1 in February 1997. Commenters call it a trendsetting trackmo with loud, energetic music and a parallax chess zoomer.

quote.text: one of my favourite demos ever. watching it now, it still gives me that same energy kick as it did the first time i saw it, almost 30 years ago!

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII story demo for the C64, third in the C64 Demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Goto80 did the music, Mathman the code and acidT*rroreast the graphics and story.
why: Commenters like the live-drawn PETSCII art, which stays in time with the music. A couple say it changed their view of PETSCII. It was reviewed in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: My favourite from the competition. So simple and so much style.

summary: Otomata Labs' Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2026. It's tagged 32k. Natt did code, graphics and music, with more code from AArt1256 and artёmka.
why: A compo winner with a six-person credit list, including graphics by Grongy and music by Enfys and nIkO.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. HCL did code and graphics, Jackasser code, Archmage, Jailbird and Dane graphics, and Dane and RaveGuru the music.
why: Axis calls it the deserved winner. Others enjoy the oldskool style with scrollers everywhere, plus the DYPP scroller, transparent rasterbars, a dot ball and a morphing line vector.

quote.text: I have to say this is the deserved winner. There is so much cool stuff in this.

summary: Bauknecht's demo for the C16/Plus 4, third in the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Mad did the code, Sire the music and graphics and Decca more graphics.
why: A podium finish on the C16/Plus 4 at the Oxyron Party.

summary: Derivative 2600 is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Mafia and Cluster, second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2015. Kylearan did the code and design and KK the music. It's tagged 32k.
why: Nominated in the That's not Possible on this Platform category at the Meteoriks 2016.

summary: Digital Mafia's Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. KK is credited with code, music and the idea.
why: A compo winner made by one person.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Xenium 2024 and nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2025. It uses the Sparkle loader. Luke and Wacek did the code, Biter and Bimber the graphics and Jammer the music.
why: Commenters see it as a worthy sequel to E2IRA and praise Jammer's soundtrack and the design. They single out the dithered landscape with motion blur and the shadow-casting rubber cube.

quote.text: Not a single second wasted here, pure killer parts from top to bottom.
